ExperimentMeta.title: ExperimentMeta
ExperimentMeta.description: Metadata about the experiment, including the random seed and stimuli versions.

id.description: Unique identifier for the experiment metadata.

seed.description: Random seed used for condition assignment.

stimuliVersion.description: Version of the stimuli used in the experiment.

lexiconVersion.description: Version of the lexicon used in the experiment.

Participant.title: Participant
Participant.description: Data for a single participant in the experiment.

conditionAssignment.description: The condition assigned to the participant.

consentTimestamp.description: Timestamp of when the participant provided consent.

consentFormVersion.description: Version of the consent form used.

userAgent.description: The user agent of the user who took the survey.

Response.title: Response
Response.description: A single response from a participant.

questionId.description: Identifier for the question this is a response to.

value.description: The participant's answer to the question.  This may be encrypted PII.

timestamp.description: Timestamp of when the response was recorded.

DerivedComposite.title: DerivedComposite
DerivedComposite.description: A computed composite score derived from multiple responses.

id.description: Unique identifier for the derived composite.

name.description: Name of the derived composite (e.g., DQ_SUB_MEAN).

value.description: The computed value of the derived composite.

timestamp.description: Timestamp of when the composite was computed.

itemsUsed.description: References to Response documents used in the composite calculation.

completenessPercentage.description: Percentage of required items that were available for computation.

DataQualityFlag.title: DataQualityFlag
DataQualityFlag.description: Flags indicating potential data quality issues.

id.description: Unique identifier for the data quality flag.

flagComprehension.description: Flag indicating potential issues with comprehension.

flagViewtime.description: Flag indicating potential issues with view time.

id.description: Unique identifier for the audit log entry.

adminId.description: Identifier of the admin performing the action.

timestamp.description: Timestamp of when the action was performed.

ObjectiveLinguisticAnalysis.title: ObjectiveLinguisticAnalysis
ObjectiveLinguisticAnalysis.description: Objective linguistic analysis of text responses.

id.description: Unique identifier for the linguistic analysis.

lexicalCategoryRates.description: Computed lexical category rates (serialized, e.g., JSON).

id.description: Unique identifier for the manual coding.

code.description: The code assigned by the coder.

firestore.reasoning:
This Firestore structure is designed to support the Advisory Insights Platform's data model and security requirements, prioritizing Authorization Independence, Clarity, and QAPs. The design uses path-based ownership and denormalization to minimize `get()` calls in security rules and ensure data integrity.

**Authorization Independence:**  Authorization independence is achieved through denormalization.  There is no use of `get()` in the security model.

**Structural Segregation:** The structure segregates data with different access requirements into separate collections, each with a homogeneous security posture.  All collections are clearly named and follow consistent naming conventions.

**Access Modeling:** Path-based ownership is employed for user-related data. For collaborative data or cases where group access is needed, a Membership Map (`members` field) would typically be used, but this application does not require collaborative data.

**Data Clarity:** Data clarity is enhanced through explicit state modeling (e.g., using a `status` field where applicable), predictable schemas, and radical consistency in naming conventions.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):** The structure enables secure `list` operations by avoiding hierarchical authorization dependencies and using appropriate data segregation. Private data resides in user-owned paths (e.g., `/users/{userId}/responses/{responseId}`), ensuring that listing responses is secure and efficient.

**Admin Access Control:** Admin audit logs are stored in a dedicated collection (`/admin_audit_logs`) to provide an auditable record of admin actions.  Admin roles (if needed) can be stored in a `/roles_admin/{uid}` collection, leveraging existence checks for authorization rules.
